lines.japanese: 寒さが今年のピークに達した、ある二月の朝だった。
lines.english: It was one February morning, on the coldest day of the year.

lines.japanese: 「うう、寒いよう、寒い寒い。このままでは凍え死んでしまう。ああ寒い、身も心も寒い」
lines.english: “Brrr, it's cold. So cold, so cold. I'm going to freeze to death. God, it's cold. My body and heart are both cold.”

lines.japanese: 今日は土曜日だ。いつまでもふとんの中で丸まっていたい衝動に駆られる。だが、そんな軟弱なことは言っていられない。
lines.english: It was Saturday. I was possessed by the urge to stay curled up under the covers forever. But I could not afford such weakness.

lines.japanese: 何故なら俺は受験生。
lines.english: For I was preparing for my entrance exams.

lines.japanese: そう、俺の受験戦争はまだ終わっていない……どころか、まさにいま佳境を迎えているのだ。奈落の名に懸けて、怠惰な弱音を吐いておる暇などないわ、るふう。
lines.english: Indeed, my war of examinations was far from over. It was, in fact, reaching its very climax. In the name of the abyss, I have no time to voice indolent complaints. Hrrfoo.

lines.japanese: 「はー、しょーがないだでねー。とりあえず顔でも洗ってこよ──」
lines.english: “Well, it can't be helped. Guess I'll start by washing my face—”

lines.japanese: 「──うおっ、なんだこの寒さ、ふざけんじゃねえブッ殺すぞココココノヤロロ」
lines.english: “—whoa! What is this cold? Fuck this! I'll k-k-k-kill you, a-asshole!”

lines.japanese: 俺はがたがたと震える体に布団を巻きつけた。
lines.english: I wrapped the covers around my shivering body.

lines.japanese: いや、そういうのはよくないよ。まず頑張って立ちあがらないかぎり、いつまで経っても眠気は消えないと思うんだ。はいはい、分かりましたよ。ったく、うるせーなあ俺は。少しは俺を見習えよな、俺。
lines.english: No, this was bad. Unless I made the effort to stand up, the drowsiness would never leave me. Yes, yes. I understood. God, I was so annoying. I should learn from me for once, me.

lines.japanese: 俺に促されて、俺は布団にくるまったまま、俺と一緒にのろのろ一階へ下りていった。
lines.english: Urged on by me, I remained wrapped in the covers and shuffled downstairs together with myself.
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 洗面所へ向かう途中、玄関で見慣れぬ靴が二組ちょこんと並んでいるのに気付いた。
lines.english: On the way to the bathroom, I noticed two unfamiliar pairs of shoes neatly lined up in the entryway.

lines.japanese: いかにも可愛らしい女の子モノ。小鳩が友達でも連れてきてるのかな。
lines.english: They were unmistakably cute girls' shoes. Had Kobato brought some friends over?

lines.japanese: しかし客の靴はふたり分なんだよな。
lines.english: But there were shoes for two guests.

lines.japanese: ひとりは吉川さんだとして、小鳩が彼女以外の友達を連れてきたことなんか今まであったっけ？
lines.english: One must belong to Yoshikawa. Had Kobato ever brought home another friend besides her?

lines.japanese: 友達少ないもんなあ、あいつ……。
lines.english: She didn't have many friends...

lines.japanese: なにしろうちの小鳩は、容姿も性格もセンス他いろいろも、およそ人間としてパーフェクト過ぎる超絶美少女だ。
lines.english: After all, our Kobato was such a transcendentally beautiful girl that her looks, personality, sense of style, and countless other qualities made her almost too perfect to be human.

lines.japanese: だから、どうしたって周囲からは嫉妬の対象として見られてしまうらしく（注：理由は俺の推測です）、交友関係もそのせいであまり広くないようなのだ。あの子ぐらい完璧だと色々あるんだね。
lines.english: That apparently made her an inevitable target of jealousy from those around her. (Note: This motive is my own conjecture.) It also seemed to have limited her social circle. Being as perfect as she was came with its share of problems.

lines.japanese: まあ、でも、金と男と自己主張が生き甲斐のビッチな糞アマに懐かれるよりはマシってことで──
lines.english: Still, that was better than having some bitch whose whole life revolved around money, men, and making herself heard latch on to her—

lines.japanese: 「──はっ！　も、もしや小鳩の可愛さに目を付けた肉食系不細工が、おこぼれに与ろうとミーハー合コンを持ちかけに来たのでは！？」
lines.english: “—wait! What if some aggressive ugly woman noticed how cute Kobato is and came to invite her to a trashy group date so she could pick up the leftovers?!”

lines.japanese: い、いかんぞ。そんな破廉恥な集会に、むざむざ俺の妹を赴かせてなるものか。プリンセス・ダヴの平和は私が守る！
lines.english: Th-this could not stand. I would never allow my little sister to attend such a shameless gathering. I shall protect the peace of Princess Dove!

lines.japanese: 俺は布団をいっそう強く巻きつけ、そろりと居間へ忍びよった。
lines.english: I wrapped the covers more tightly around myself and crept toward the living room.

lines.japanese: 『まあ、見てくださいこの指輪。素敵ですねー、こんな指輪プレゼントされちゃったら、女性はみんなクラッときちゃいますよねー』
lines.english: “My, look at this ring. Isn't it lovely? Any woman would go weak in the knees if someone gave her a ring like this.”

lines.japanese: テレビの音が漏れているふすまに耳をそばだててみる。女子アナのコメントに被さって、少女たちの声が交錯していた。
lines.english: I pressed my ear to the sliding door, through which the television could be heard. Several girls' voices overlapped the announcer's commentary.

lines.japanese: 「このひと、いつもおんなじこと言ってる」
lines.english: “That lady always says the same thing.”

lines.japanese: ひとつは心の洗われる天使の鐘、すなわち小鳩の声だ。
lines.english: One was an angel's bell that cleansed the heart—in other words, Kobato's voice.

lines.japanese: 「羽田さん羽田さん、こんなのどうかな。あー、でも作るの難しそう」
lines.english: “Haneda, Haneda, how about this one? Oh, but it looks hard to make.”

lines.japanese: もうひとつは、小鳩の親友・吉川さんのもの。
lines.english: Another belonged to Kobato's best friend, Yoshikawa.

lines.japanese: 「私は思います、挑戦する価値はあると」
lines.english: “I think it worth attempting, this.”

lines.japanese: 残るひとつ、この特徴的な日本語はアリスか。
lines.english: The last voice spoke its characteristic Japanese. That would be Alice.

lines.japanese: ああ、そういえばあいつ、年末ぐらいからときどき小鳩たちと遊ぶようになってたな。
lines.english: Oh, right. Since around the end of the year, she had occasionally started spending time with Kobato and her friends.

lines.japanese: うむ、うちの妹と仲良くしたがるなんて、あの国の人間はなかなか見所があるようだ。
lines.english: Hmm. Anyone from that country who wished to befriend my sister clearly possessed an excellent eye.

lines.japanese: まあ、なんにせよ、小鳩が図々しい不細工に狙われてなくて良かった良かった。
lines.english: At any rate, I was relieved that no brazen ugly woman had set her sights on Kobato.

lines.japanese: 俺はふすまの向こうでこたつを囲んでいる少女たちを思いうかべて、ほのぼのと目を細めるのだった。
lines.english: Imagining the girls gathered around the kotatsu beyond the door, I narrowed my eyes with warm affection.

lines.japanese: しかし、作るとか難しそうとか、いったい何の話をしてるんだろう。
lines.english: But what were they talking about making, and why did it sound difficult?

lines.japanese: 気になるな。ちょっとだけ開けて、こっそり覗い……あ、いや、見守ってあげよう。
lines.english: I was curious. I would open the door just a crack and secretly peek... No, watch over them.

lines.japanese: 「羽田さん、これとかどう？　え、えーと、ざ、ざっはとるて？　こんなの私も食べてみたい」
lines.english: “Haneda, how about this? Um, s-sack-er tort? I'd like to try it too.”

lines.japanese: 「私はとても同感に思う。私も好む、Ｓａｃｈｅｒ　Ｔｏｒｔｅを」
lines.english: “I agree very strongly. I also like Sacher torte.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、でもこっちの、ぶ、ぶるぼんぬ？　……先生がえらんだ、冴子流かがやく私のモテかわスイーツも美味しそうだよ」
lines.english: “Oh, but these look good too: ‘Saeko’s Radiant Popular-Cute Sweets,’ selected by Madame Bur... Bourbonne?”

lines.japanese: ほうほう？　どうやら女の子向け雑誌でも開きながら、手作り菓子談義でもしてるみたいだ。
lines.english: Hmm, hmm. Apparently, they were looking through a magazine for girls and discussing homemade sweets.

lines.japanese: ああ、年頃の女の子はそういうのが好きだからなあ。うんうん、微笑ましいなあ。
lines.english: Girls that age loved such things. Yes, yes. How sweet.

lines.japanese: 中でも小鳩がいちばん微笑ましいなあ。アリスや吉川さんもなかなかに微笑ましいけど、さすがに小鳩には敵わないもんなあ。
lines.english: Kobato was by far the sweetest of them. Alice and Yoshikawa were fairly sweet too, but naturally, neither could compare with Kobato.

lines.japanese: 「このＣｈｏｃｏｌａｔｅ　ｃａｋｅは食べられた、かつて私に。その後、私はしばしばこの味に焦がれている」
lines.english: “This chocolate cake was once eaten by me. Since then, I have often longed for this taste.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、アリスちゃん食べたことあるんだ。そ、それはうらまやしい……」
lines.english: “What? You’ve had it before, Alice? Th-that makes me so jealious...”

lines.japanese: 「羽田さん、そしたらこのケーキ作ろうよ。えへへ、アリスちゃんに来てもらってよかったね」
lines.english: “Then let's make this cake, Haneda. Hee-hee. It's a good thing we invited Alice.”

lines.japanese: 「うんっ！　じゃあキッチン行こ」
lines.english: “Yeah! Let's go to the kitchen.”

lines.japanese: げっ、こっち出てくるのか。
lines.english: Crap. They were coming this way.

lines.japanese: 俺はそれまで纏っていた掛け布団を、階段の上へえいやと放りなげた。
lines.english: I threw the comforter I had been wearing up the stairs with a mighty heave.

lines.japanese: 「あれっ、お兄ちゃん？　もう起きてきたんだ、えへっ、おはよー」
lines.english: “Oh, Big Brother? You're up already. Hee-hee. Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 「わわっ、お、お兄さん！　お、おお、おはようございますっ」
lines.english: “Wah! M-mister! G-good morning!”

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、おはよう。よく来たな、私はたいへん歓迎をします」
lines.english: “Good morning, Dora. You have come at a good time. I welcome you greatly.”

lines.japanese: ふすまを開いて現れた少女たちは、俺の登場を口々に喜んでくれた。
lines.english: The girls emerged through the sliding door and each expressed her delight at my arrival.

lines.japanese: ああ、なんて可愛い子たちなんだろう。
lines.english: What adorable girls they were.

lines.japanese: しかし、とりわけ小鳩がいちばん可愛いなあ。ああ、拝みたくなるほどの可愛さだ。ほろぼろしい、ほろぼろしい。
lines.english: Kobato, in particular, was the most adorable. Adorable enough to worship. So adorably divine. So adorably divine.

lines.japanese: あっ！　でも俺べつに、シスコンとかロリコンとかそういうの全然ないけどね！
lines.english: Oh! Not that I had a sister complex or any interest in little girls!

lines.japanese: 「やあ、みんなおはよう。今日もいい朝だね、ははは」
lines.english: “Good morning, everyone. Another beautiful morning, ha-ha-ha.”

lines.japanese: 「でもお兄ちゃん、なんでそんな寒そうな格好？」
lines.english: “But Big Brother, won’t you be cold dressed like that?”

lines.japanese: さっきまで布団アーマーを装備していた俺は、いまやエマージェンシー・クロースアウトしてＴシャツ一枚という軽装だった。
lines.english: Until moments ago, I had been equipped with comforter armor. Now, after an emergency clothes-out, I wore the light gear of a single T-shirt.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、冬だからと言って怠けちゃいけないからね。こうして薄着になることで、自らに喝を入れているというわけさ、ぐ、ぐれっす！　ぐれっす！　ぐれすぴあ！」
lines.english: “Winter is no excuse for laziness. By dressing lightly, I give my spirit a firm rebuke. Gr-greth! Greth! Grethpia!”

lines.japanese: 「わあ、お兄さんって個性的なくしゃみするんですね」
lines.english: “Wow, you have a very distinctive sneeze, mister.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　あ、あはは、まあね……」
lines.english: “What? Oh, ah-ha-ha. I suppose...”

lines.japanese: いかんいかん、ちょっと油断して、伽楼羅のグレタガルド風邪とかいう妄想設定が日常に漏れでてしまった。
lines.english: This was bad. My guard had slipped, and Karura's imaginary Gretagardian cold had leaked into everyday life.

lines.japanese: 統合前の固有の人格が、意図もせず前面に出るこんな状況は好ましくない。
lines.english: I did not want the distinct personalities from before our integration unintentionally pushing their way to the front like this.

lines.japanese: まさかまた仮統合のネジが緩んでるわけじゃないだろうが、気は引きしめないとな。
lines.english: Surely the screws holding our provisional integration together had not come loose again, but I needed to remain vigilant.

lines.japanese: 俺はフッと息を吹きあげて前髪を揺らした。
lines.english: I blew upward and made my bangs flutter.

lines.japanese: 「ところでこの集まりはなんだ？　いま叔父さんも叔母さんも出かけてるみたいだけど、今日みんなが来ることは言ってあるのか？」
lines.english: “By the way, what is this gathering? My aunt and uncle appear to be out. Did you tell them everybody was coming today?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　なに言ってんの？　お父さんとお母さんきょう社交ダンス行くって、きのう言ってたでしょ」
lines.english: “What? What are you talking about? Mom and Dad said yesterday they were going ballroom dancing today.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだっけ？」
lines.english: “Oh. Did they?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ～？　ごはんのときお兄ちゃんも聞いてたよう。お父さんにサルサで勝負挑んでたもん」
lines.english: “What? You heard them at dinner. You challenged Dad to a salsa battle.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: うそだ、そんな記憶ないぞ。
lines.english: That wasn't true. I had no memory of such a thing.

lines.japanese: いや、でも、よい子の小鳩がそんな嘘をつく必要はないだろうし、冗談……を言ってる感じでもないか。
lines.english: But good little Kobato had no reason to lie, and she did not appear to be joking either.

lines.japanese: どういうことだ、こりゃ。俺は後ろ頭をがしがし掻いた。
lines.english: What was going on? I scratched hard at the back of my head.

lines.japanese: 「あ、それじゃお兄ちゃん、朝ごはんすぐ準備するから待っててね」
lines.english: “Oh, Big Brother, I'll make your breakfast right away. Just wait here.”
“Y-yeah...”

lines.japanese: ぱたぱたと小鳩はキッチンへ向かい、少女ふたりもその後に続いた。
lines.english: Kobato hurried into the kitchen, and the other two girls followed.

lines.japanese: 俺の目はその背中を見送っていたが、頭ではまったく違うことを考えていた。
lines.english: My eyes watched their backs, but my mind was occupied by something entirely different.

lines.japanese: 記憶の喪失、混乱──
lines.english: Missing memories. Confusion—

lines.japanese: ──それらは仮統合以来ときおり起こる、不具合の前兆だ。
lines.english: —these were signs of the malfunctions that had occasionally occurred since our provisional integration.

lines.japanese: 「このままじゃまずいな……」
lines.english: “This is bad...”

lines.japanese: 居間で小鳩の用意してくれた朝食を摂りながら、俺は意識の安定化に努めていた。
lines.english: As I sat in the living room eating the breakfast Kobato had made for me, I worked to stabilize my consciousness.

lines.japanese: 「まずい……なんとかしなければ……」
lines.english: “Bad... I have to do something...”

lines.japanese: 「へっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「まま、不味かった、でしたか……」
lines.english: “W-was it bad...?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、非常にまずい」
lines.english: “Yeah. Extremely bad.”

lines.japanese: 「うえっ！？　ごごごごめんなさい」
lines.english: “Wha?! I-I'm sorry!”

lines.japanese: 「まいったな、こいつはマジでやばい。頭がどうにかなりそうだ」
lines.english: “Damn it, this is seriously bad. I feel like I'm losing my mind.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなにも！？」
lines.english: “It's that bad?!”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……まずいまずい、これはほっとくわけいかないぞ」
lines.english: “Yeah... Bad, bad. I can't just leave this alone.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい、すぐ作りなおしてくるます！」
lines.english: “O-okay! I'll make it again right now!”

lines.japanese: 「へ……？　あっ、おい小鳩！　お兄ちゃんまだ食べてる途中だぞ、勝手に持ってかないでくれ」
lines.english: “Huh...? Hey, Kobato! Your big brother's still eating. Don't take it away without asking.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、でも……」
「いやあ、それにしても小鳩の作るごはんはいつもいつも美味しいなあ」
lines.english: “Honestly, everything Kobato cooks is always so delicious.”

lines.japanese: 「ふへ？　何それ、言ってること違う」
lines.english: “Huh? What? Now you're saying the opposite.”

lines.japanese: 「まいったな、こいつはマジで美味いぞ。頭がどうにかなりそうだ」
lines.english: “Damn, this is seriously good. I feel like I'm losing my mind.”

lines.japanese: 「お、落として上げるは上級者の手口です」
lines.english: “T-tearing somebody down and then lifting them up is an advanced technique.”

lines.japanese: 「なにが？　いや、だって美味いじゃん小鳩の料理」
lines.english: “What is? I'm telling you, your food's delicious.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなことないって、えへへ」
lines.english: “N-no, it isn't. Hee-hee.”

lines.japanese: 「小鳩。私は戻ってきてほしい、キッチンへ」
lines.english: “Kobato. I want you to return to the kitchen.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、うん、いま行くー」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Coming!”

lines.japanese: ケーキ作りのため、小鳩は友人たちの待つ台所へ向かった。
lines.english: Kobato headed for the kitchen, where her friends were waiting to make the cake.
“Phew...”

lines.japanese: 俺は箸を休める。
lines.english: I set down my chopsticks.

lines.japanese: 小鳩の料理が美味いのは揺るぎない事実だが、不吉な予兆が食欲を抑制してしまう。
lines.english: Kobato's cooking was unquestionably delicious, but the ominous signs had suppressed my appetite.

lines.japanese: すなわち──
lines.english: They were signs—

lines.japanese: ──統合が解けてしまう、予兆。
lines.english: —that our integration was coming undone.
